investigator.method: Bounded Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC investigation per BOTM-LONDON-SECOND-LIVE-TRANCHE-01: one unauthenticated GET to the venue's official_website (WebFetch/curl fallback), with at most one additional same-origin GET when official_programme_url was directly supplied as a candidate field. No browser, authentication, CAPTCHA bypass, or retry loop.

venue_reference: Jako London — Kensington High Street 1, W8 5NP, London

identity.notes: The requested official_website 301-redirects cross-domain to https://www.casajako.com/, and casajako.com's own canonical link and og:description self-locate it as 'a private-hire venue in Holborn, Central London' — a different area of London from the candidate's discovery address ('Kensington High Street 1, W8 5NP'). This bounded probe cannot determine whether Casa Jako is genuinely the same business as the OSM-sourced 'Jako London' candidate (relocated/rebranded) or an unrelated business now occupying that redirect target; identity is not proven.

site_classification.platform: Wix site (redirect target casajako.com); acquisition path cannot be honestly classified while identity itself is unresolved.

blockers.description: Identity is unresolved: the official_website redirects cross-domain to a page self-locating in Holborn, not Kensington (the candidate's discovery address). This must be resolved by a human before any further work on this candidate.

probe_history.reason: The single unauthenticated GET to the supplied official_website returned a genuine HTTP 301 cross-domain redirect to casajako.com, whose own retained content self-locates the business in Holborn — a different part of London from the candidate's discovery address. This is not a technical access-control block, but it is a legitimate boundary this bounded Level-1 probe cannot safely resolve on its own: continuing to treat casajako.com as this candidate's authoritative site would risk silently substituting one business's facts for another's, which policy prohibits.

reasons: https://www.jakolondon.com/ issues a real HTTP 301 redirect to https://www.casajako.com/, and Casa Jako's own canonical link, og:title ('Private Hire Venue Holborn | Casa Jako'), and og:description self-locate the business in Holborn, Central London — not Kensington High Street, the candidate's discovery address.

This bounded, single-GET probe cannot determine whether this is a genuine same-business rebrand/relocation or an unrelated business now controlling the domain; per policy, an investigation must never silently treat a redirect target as proven identity without evidence, so identity is recorded as AMBIGUOUS rather than PROVEN.

Independently, the redirect target self-describes as a private-hire events venue ('ideal for small to large events, club nights, ticketed events, birthdays and corporate receptions') rather than a self-programmed venue, which would itself complicate a straightforward music-gate determination even if identity were resolved.

evidence.description: Retained HTTP response headers showing a genuine 301 Moved Permanently cross-domain redirect from jakolondon.com to casajako.com.
evidence.method: curl -sS -L; descriptive User-Agent; single unauthenticated GET; redirects followed and recorded; no retry

evidence.description: Verbatim, byte-faithful excerpt of the redirect target's <head>: canonical link and og:title/og:description, self-locating the business in Holborn, Central London.
evidence.method: curl -sS -L; descriptive User-Agent; same single unauthenticated GET, redirect followed automatically; no retry
